newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland pares snowstorm power outages.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland pares snowstorm power outages.

text.p: Cleveland Electric Illuminating Co (CEI) was still reducing snow-related power outages as snow continued to blanket parts of its Ohio service territory.
"We still have 8,000 (customers) out," said CEI spokeswoman Irene Prezelj.
The utility, a subsidiary of Centerior Energy Corp, cut the number of customer outages from 20,000 on Tuesday.
Although snowfall stopped in Cleveland, precipitation continued in counties east of the city with accumulation hitting the four foot mark in some areas, Prezelj said.
"They'll have another eight inches today," she said.

Efforts to resume power service in those eastern counties have been slowed because of new outages caused by non-stop snowfall. But CEI still aimed to return electricity to all remaining customers by Wednesday, she said.
"We're planning to restore a majority of those customers by the end of the day," Prezelj said.
She said 350 repair crews, including those from its sister company Toledo Edison Co, Ohio Edison Co, and American Electric Power Co, continued to clear fallen trees and repair down power lines.
